title: Disaster at Cannae
objective: After this level you can explain what happened at Cannae and why it is still studied.
summary: At Cannae in 216 BCE Hannibal encircled a much larger Roman army and destroyed it. Rome lost tens of thousands, yet refused to make peace.

cards.headline: A much larger Roman army walked into a trap it couldn’t escape.
cards.body: More soldiers usually means a better chance. At Cannae, Hannibal made Rome’s numbers work against it.

cards.headline: The trap
cards.body: At Cannae in 216 BCE, Hannibal faced a much larger Roman army. He let the center of his line fall back as the Romans pushed forward, so every step forward carried them deeper in. Then his wings and cavalry closed around them from both sides. The army doing the pushing was suddenly surrounded. This is a double envelopment: think of a hand closing into a fist, with the Romans inside.
cards.callout: Center falls back, wings close in

cards.headline: A catastrophe, and a refusal
cards.body: Ancient sources report Roman losses in the tens of thousands, one of the worst defeats in Roman history. After a blow like that, you’d expect Rome to ask for terms. It refused to make peace. Hannibal had won a battle. He had not won the war. Officers still study Cannae as the classic example of encirclement. Rome was the first to learn that lesson, the hard way.

cards.headline: Cannae: studied
learned: He encircled a larger Roman army
Rome still refused to make peace

questions.prompt: The Battle of Cannae was fought in _____.

options.label: 264 BCE
options.rationale: That’s when the Punic Wars began.

questions.explanation: Hannibal destroyed a Roman army at Cannae in 216 BCE.

questions.prompt: Put Hannibal’s trap at Cannae in order, from first to last.
questions.explanation: Hannibal’s center fell back as the Romans pushed, then his wings and cavalry closed in, and the Roman army was suddenly surrounded.

questions.prompt: From Level 23: how had Hannibal’s army reached Italy before Cannae?

options.label: By a secret treaty with Rome
By marching over the Alps from Spain

questions.explanation: Hannibal crossed the Alps from Spain in 218 BCE, two years before Cannae.
